newsitem.title: FRANCE: French car sales surge in August.
newsitem.headline: French car sales surge in August.

text.p: French car sales raced ahead in August as consumers stepped up purchases ahead of the expiry this month of a government rebate offer, the French carmakers association CCFA said on Monday.
Sales of new cars in France surged 29.4 percent last month from weak August 1995 levels to 172,400, it said.

"These good results -- one needs to go back to August 1990 to find a higher level of sales -- reflect the start of the acceleration of orders ahead of the conclusion of the 'quality rebates' on September 30," it said in a statement.
More than 30 percent of the new car orders in August were tied to the rebates of between 5,000 francs ($985) and 7,000 francs for buyers turning in old clunkers.
However, the CCFA said the rise also reflected the poor prior-year sales following the expiry on June 30, 1995, of a previous rebate scheme. Car sales plummeted after its expiry.
On a comparable-day basis -- there were 21 working days last month compared with 22 in August 1995 -- the rise in new car sales was 35.5 percent, the CCFA said.

The results were positive for French carmakers, which have lost market share at home in recent months despite the rollout of new models such as the sleek Peugeot 406, the small Citroen Saxo and the innovative Renault Megane.
The PSA Peugeot Citroen group's car sales rose 25.6 percent in August from year-earlier levels, while Renault SA sales climbed 29.3 percent.
Their shares rose on the news. PSA's stock was up three francs at 583 at 1210 GMT, while Renault shares were up one franc at 113.30.
Sales of foreign cars in France rose 31.7 percent from year-earlier levels for a combined market share of 47.7 percent.
In the first eight months of 1995, car sales in France totalled 1.44 million, up 7.4 percent from the year-earlier period.
Car sales by French manufacturers were down 1.2 percent over the eight-month period, while sales by foreign rivals rose 20.4 percent.

The biggest gainers were Italy's Fiat, whose sales rose 47 percent, boosted by a weak lira and the success of its new Bravo/Brava models, and Volkswagen, whose sales in France rose 24 percent over the January-August period.
